marker.description: Blue-headed pin inserted into the white matter of the frontal lobe

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the blue pin.
main_explanation: The blue pin is inserted into the large, C-shaped band of white matter that connects the left and right cerebral hemispheres. In a mid-sagittal section, this structure is the corpus callosum.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following is a primary function of the structure indicated?
options: Communication between the left and right cerebral hemispheres
supporting_question.explanation: The corpus callosum is the largest commissure in the brain, consisting of white matter fibers that allow for the transfer of information and communication between the two cerebral hemispheres.

true_false.statement: The structure indicated is composed primarily of grey matter.
true_false.explanation: The corpus callosum is composed of white matter (myelinated axons), which appear lighter in color compared to the grey matter of the cortex.
